title: Golden Sequins, Red Boots, and 200 Dancers: The Last Great Bhansali Song Is Being Shot Right Now
excerpt: Fresh set images from 'Love & War' confirm what everyone suspected — Sanjay Leela Bhansali's climactic song sequence is going to be the most extravagant Bollywood number of the year.
body:
Somewhere inside Royal Palms Studio in Mumbai this week, Sanjay Leela Bhansali is doing what he does better than anyone alive: building a world one sequin at a time.

Fresh set images from Love & War have surfaced, and they confirm what anyone who's followed Bhansali's career already suspected — the man's final song sequence for this film is going to be staggering. Alia Bhatt was spotted heading toward her vanity van in a golden sequined mini skirt, a bright red scarf thrown over her shoulders, and matching red boots that screamed vintage glamour with modern heat. Vicky Kaushal kept it classic — a black shirt and trousers layered under a grey coat — understated next to Alia's shimmer, but sharp enough to hold the frame. The costumes alone tell you this isn't some throwaway number being filmed to pad a soundtrack album. This is a Bhansali song. The kind that opens festivals and wins national awards and lives rent-free in your head for years.

Ranbir Kapoor, the film's third lead, was notably absent from the set that day, though reports confirm he has been part of the shoot across earlier sessions.

!Sanjay Leela Bhansali — Photo: Wikimedia Commons

"When your director's definition of "preparation" involves constructing entire worlds on a soundstage and dressing two hundred bodies in period-accurate clothing, delays aren't setbacks."

According to Mid-Day, the sequence features nearly 200 dancers alongside the three leads, and Bhansali spent weeks perfecting the choreography, costumes, and production design before rolling a single camera. Every frame has reportedly been storyboarded in advance — which is why the shoot was pushed back by two weeks from its original June 8 start date. When your director's definition of "preparation" involves constructing entire worlds on a soundstage and dressing two hundred bodies in period-accurate clothing, delays aren't setbacks. They're standards.

"It's being designed as a spectacle. The choreography, costumes, and production design have been in preparation for weeks. The scale is enormous, even by Bhansali standards. Every frame has been meticulously storyboarded." — Production insider to Mid-Day

This is the climactic song of Love & War, and by the sound of it, Bhansali is pouring everything he has into the sequence. The film is already approximately 90 per cent complete, with this elaborate number designed as the centrepiece — the kind of large-scale musical spectacle that Bhansali has made synonymous with his name, from the mirrored grandeur of Devdas' "Maar Dala" to the operatic sweep of Bajirao Mastani's "Deewani Mastani" to the raw, earthy power of Gangubai Kathiawadi's title track.

!Mumbai — Photo: Wikimedia Commons

The film itself is one of the most anticipated releases in recent Bollywood memory. It brings together Ranbir Kapoor and Alia Bhatt — married in real life, reuniting on screen for the first time since Brahmastra — alongside Vicky Kaushal, who's been quietly assembling one of the most impressive filmographies of his generation. The three are playing characters in a war-set love triangle, which is about as Bhansali as a premise can get: sweeping romance, grand conflict, and the question of what love costs when the world is falling apart.

Ranbir returns to a Bhansali set for the first time since his debut film Saawariya, nearly two decades ago. Alia reunites with the director who turned her into an awards magnet with Gangubai Kathiawadi. And for Vicky, this is a career dream materialised.

"It's on the bucket list of every actor to be a part of a Sanjay Leela Bhansali film. He truly is a master of the craft of filmmaking. I genuinely feel blessed that in just ten years of my career I got to work with him." — Vicky Kaushal

The production has weathered its share of delays. Originally aimed at an Eid 2026 release, then pushed to summer, Love & War is now locked for January 21, 2027 — a pan-India release in Hindi, Tamil, and Telugu that perfectly catches Republic Day weekend. Bhansali's films have always played beautifully with NRI audiences. Padmaavat was a diaspora phenomenon, Gangubai pulled massive overseas numbers, and Love & War, with its three A-list leads and characteristically lavish mounting, is expected to be an even bigger international draw.

Until then, we have these images: Alia glittering under studio lights in gold and red, Vicky radiating quiet intensity in his tailored greys, and a director who refuses to let a single stitch go unplanned. The last great Bhansali song is being filmed right now. When it arrives on screen, you'll know it was worth every week of waiting.
